dial.summary: Seven of eight macro indicators remain constructive on August 18 — DXY fell to a 2-month low of 99.40 (neutral band, lowest since June), the 2s10s yield curve steepened further to +58bps as the 10Y rose to 4.73%, and real yields hold at 2.40% as the lone structural headwind; BTC surged 1.8% to $64,269 lifting total crypto to $2.28T with BTC dominance at 56.5%, well above the 55% Alt Rotation trigger; FOMC Minutes (August 19), Philly Fed + Jobless Claims (August 20), Flash PMI (August 21), and the decisive PCE/GDP/Jackson Hole cluster (August 26–28) are the catalyst window ahead — dial holds at BTC Accumulation.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $102,663.81B (~$102.7T) for June 2026 — most recent available (July aggregate carries a ~6-week reporting lag); US M2 rose to a record $23.16T in June 2026, +5.6% YoY (28th consecutive monthly increase); Federal Reserve H.6 for July 2026 released July 28 confirms continued US M2 expansion; global M2 growing at approximately +12% YoY based on Feb 2026 cross-bank data; 4-week trend up (US M2 expanding at 5.6% YoY, major CB aggregate YoY contraction headwind condition not triggered); status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed across major central bank aggregates; no YoY contraction signal from any major central bank).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) is the most recent reading — August 2026 data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: Production 58.5%, New Orders 56.7%, Employment 52.8% (first factory employment expansion in 33 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July reading is the highest since May 2022; Philly Fed (August 20) and Flash PMI (August 21) will provide first August manufacturing signals; 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp, seventh consecutive expansion month; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.40 (August 18, 2026 — lowest since June 2026); dollar fell for a third straight session as cooling US economic data prompted traders to price 67% probability of September Fed hold (up from below 50% a month prior); 4-week change: -1.52% (approximately 100.9 mid-July → 99.40 August 18), above the 0.5% flat threshold; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; PCE August 26 and Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 are the key directional catalysts — a dovish combination could push DXY below 97.5 into supportive territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 confirmed at 2.40% as of August 14, 2026 (most recent confirmed value; H.15 for August 18 not yet accessed); the July 23, 2026 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.438%, a 16-year high for this term; nominal 10Y Treasury rose to 4.73% on August 18 (from 4.69% August 17), keeping real yields near 2.40%; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (mid-July) → 2.40% (August 14) = +22bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% threshold; soft July PCE August 26 and/or dovish Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 are key catalysts to compress real yields toward the 2% neutral boundary).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 18, 2026: DGS10 at 4.73% (up 4bps from 4.69% on August 17); DGS2 estimated ~4.15% (last confirmed August 13); spread = +58bps (steepened from +54bps on August 17); front-end yields remain anchored as markets price 67% probability of September Fed hold on soft labor and retail data; 4-week trend up: ~35bps (mid-July) → +58bps (August 18) = +23bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening; FOMC Minutes August 19 and Warsh keynote August 28 are the next directional catalysts).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.76T for week ending August 12, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 13); up ~$60B from $6.70T for week ending August 5; next H.4.1 release (week ending August 19) due August 20; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.73T (mid-July estimate) → $6.76T (August 12) = +$30B (~+0.4%), within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT; soft July labor, retail, and benign inflation data further reduce September hike probability and near-term QT acceleration risk).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass and Coinalyze blocked by network proxy — value carried forward at +0.004%/8h; BTC surged 1.8% to $64,269 on August 18 with total crypto market cap rising 2.6% to $2.28T; BTC dominance at 56.5% (firm above the 55% Alt Rotation trigger); near-zero positive funding well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; on a risk-on day with BTC +1.8%, funding rates may tick up modestly but remain well within supportive range; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June toward near-zero); status supportive (near-zero funding signals healthy positioning without leverage crowding).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$310B (USDT ~$183.4B, USDC ~$71.9B) as of August 18, 2026; total crypto market cap $2.28T (BTC market cap ~$1.29T, BTC dominance 56.5%); stablecoin dominance 13.60% ($310B / $2.28T); 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (mid-July) → 13.60% (August 18) = -0.70pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over 30 days; today's crypto surge (+2.6%) driven by risk assets not stablecoin inflows; status supportive (30-day declining trend intact; headwind condition requires dominance rising WHILE TOTAL market also rising on a sustained basis — 30-day dominance compression of -0.70pp alongside rising TOTAL confirms capital rotation into risk, not defensive repositioning).

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (July 28–29, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the July 28–29, 2026 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — three weeks after the July 29 policy decision (held at 3.50–3.75%, 9-3 vote); by release markets will have processed July NFP (−23,000, Aug 7), hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, Aug 12), benign July PPI (Aug 13), soft July retail sales (Aug 14), Housing Starts (Aug 18), and DXY at a 2-month low of 99.40; markets now price 67% probability of September Fed hold; key signals: degree of consensus for September hike vs. hold/cut, how three dissenters characterized the inflation/labor trade-off, and any explicit forward guidance thresholds; Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (August 28) is the dominant macro catalyst following these minutes.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Philadelphia Federal Reserve Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — second August regional manufacturing read alongside weekly Jobless Claims; cross-checks July ISM surge (55.6%) against hot core CPI (3.1%), July NFP shock (−23,000), and soft July retail sales; released the day after FOMC Minutes (August 19); a positive Philly Fed reading would reinforce manufacturing resilience and sustain the BTC Accumulation dial heading into PCE (August 26) and Jackson Hole (August 27–29).

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 15, 2026 — released alongside Philly Fed survey; weekly labor read post-July NFP shock (−23,000, August 7); markets pricing 67% probability of September Fed hold; a sustained rise above 215K alongside negative NFP would deepen the stagflationary picture heading into PCE (August 26) and Jackson Hole (August 27–29), potentially strengthening the case for a September rate cut rather than a hike.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: S&P Global Flash PMI preliminary estimates for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first composite activity read for August; July 2026: Manufacturing 53.8, Services 53.6; the August read is the first broad activity gauge post-NFP shock (−23,000), hot core CPI (3.1%, August 12), FOMC Minutes (August 19), and Philly Fed (August 20); DXY at 99.40 (2-month low) and 2s10s at +58bps reflect reduced September hike probability; a soft August composite alongside weak labor and retail data would validate Q3 recession-risk concerns; a stable-to-improving read supports BTC Accumulation heading into PCE (August 26) and Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (August 28).

upcoming.title: Consumer Confidence (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released alongside New Home Sales and Richmond Fed Manufacturing; the consumer sentiment gauge incorporates July NFP shock (−23,000, August 7), hot core CPI (3.1%, August 12), soft July retail sales (August 14), Housing Starts (August 18), FOMC Minutes tone (August 19), and Flash PMI (August 21); a sharp deterioration in confidence would raise Q3 recession risk ahead of the decisive Jackson Hole–PCE cluster (August 26–28) and bolster the case for September rate cuts over hikes; DXY at 99.40 and 2s10s steepening to +58bps reflect markets already tilting toward a hold.
